title: Ait Ben Haddou
summary: Ait Ben Haddou is a fortified earthen village (ksar) in Ouarzazate province, Morocco, on the southern slopes of the High Atlas. Its oldest buildings seem no earlier than the 17th century. UNESCO inscribed it on the World Heritage List in 1987 as an example of pre-Saharan earthen architecture.

uncertainty.note: Start is the earliest century of surviving construction per Archnet (not earlier than the 17th century); end year marks the 1987 World Heritage inscription, not abandonment.

when.display: 17th century (oldest surviving buildings); World Heritage listing 1987
